facts.text: Hollis was a stop on the Worcester & Nashua Railroad, which ran through town in 1848 on a route between Worcester and Portland.
Every year the Hollis Old Home Days weekend celebrates the town’s heritage, a tradition started in 1899 by Governor Frank West Rollins.
The annual Strawberry Festival in June features a town band concert and locally grown strawberry treats like shortcake, pie, and ice‑cream.
October’s Hollis Apple Festival hosts a town band concert and showcases apple‑based foods, drawing visitors to the town’s autumn harvest.
The historic Farley Building, built in 1877, served as Hollis High School until the 2005‑2006 school year and now houses community events.
Hollis Village Historic District, listed on the National Register, preserves the town center’s 18th‑century architecture and layout.
